status: draft: needs author review before it is frozen into evaluation/benchmarks/
policy: Evidence is cited by exact quotation from the demo notes, not by chunk ID, so labels survive re-chunking. Reference answers are examples of a correct synthesis, not exact-match targets. Answer cases list the points a complete answer must express; refuse cases must be answered exactly "I don't know.".

categories.paraphrase: Asks about a fact without the notes' key words; needs semantic search.
categories.exact_term: Hinges on a precise technical term; needs keyword search.
categories.cross_note: Needs evidence from two different notes.
categories.multi_part: Several requested parts from one note; tests completeness.
categories.qualifier: Tempts the answer to drop a qualifier such as may, often or usually.
categories.near_miss_refusal: The topic is in the notes but the requested detail is not.
categories.out_of_scope: The topic is not in the notes at all.

cases.question: What can happen when the steps an optimizer takes are far too small?

required_points.text: A learning rate that is too small may result in slow convergence.

evidence.quote: A learning rate that is too small may result in slow convergence.

cases.reference_answer: If the learning rate (step size) is too small, gradient descent may converge slowly.
cases.review_notes: Preserve may. The question never says learning rate or convergence.

cases.question: What do we call choosing, reshaping and inventing the inputs a model uses from raw data?

required_points.text: This is feature engineering: selecting, transforming and creating useful features from raw data.

evidence.quote: Feature engineering is the process of selecting, transforming, and creating useful features from raw data.

cases.reference_answer: Feature engineering: selecting, transforming and creating useful features from raw data.
cases.review_notes: Naming feature engineering is the core point.

cases.question: Which transformation makes every input have an average of zero and a spread of one?

required_points.text: Standardization transforms values to zero mean and unit variance.

evidence.quote: Standardization transforms values so they have zero mean and unit variance.

cases.reference_answer: Standardization, which transforms values to have zero mean and unit variance.
cases.review_notes: Must not answer normalization, which rescales to a range.

cases.question: My report used numbers that another user had changed but then cancelled before saving. Which concurrency problem is this?

required_points.text: This is a dirty read: reading data written by another transaction that has not yet committed.

evidence.quote: A dirty read happens when a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed.

cases.reference_answer: A dirty read: a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed.
cases.review_notes: The name alone is not enough; the uncommitted-data mechanism is required.

cases.question: Two people edit the same record at the same time and one person's change silently disappears. What is this called?

required_points.text: This is a lost update: one transaction overwrites the result of another.

evidence.quote: A lost update occurs when one transaction overwrites the result of another.

cases.reference_answer: A lost update, where one transaction overwrites the result of another.
cases.review_notes: Name and mechanism both required.

cases.question: Why is switching between two separate running programs slower than switching between two workers inside the same program?

required_points.text: Switching between processes is generally more expensive than switching between threads.

evidence.quote: Context switching between processes is generally more expensive than switching between threads because more state must be saved and restored.
Creating and switching between processes is generally more expensive than creating and switching between threads because processes require more operating system overhead.

required_points.text: Because more state must be saved and restored (more operating system overhead).

evidence.quote: because more state must be saved and restored
because processes require more operating system overhead

cases.reference_answer: Switching between processes is generally more expensive than switching between threads, because more state must be saved and restored and processes require more operating-system overhead.
cases.review_notes: Either reason satisfies the reason point. Preserve generally.

cases.question: What do you call a model that is too simple and does badly even on the data it learned from?

required_points.text: This is underfitting: the model is too simple to capture patterns in the training data.

evidence.quote: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture patterns in the training data.
A model that performs poorly even on training data may be underfitting.

cases.reference_answer: Underfitting: the model is too simple to capture the patterns in the training data, so it performs poorly even there.
cases.review_notes: Naming underfitting with its meaning is required.

cases.question: What is it called when one large table is split into several smaller ones while keeping what the data means?

required_points.text: Decomposition splits a table into smaller relations while preserving data meaning.

evidence.quote: Decomposition is often used to split such a table into smaller relations while preserving data meaning.

cases.reference_answer: Decomposition, which splits a table into smaller relations while preserving data meaning.
cases.review_notes: The question avoids the words relation, decompose and normalization.

cases.question: What kind of learning uses examples that each come with the correct answer attached?

required_points.text: Supervised learning, in which a model learns from labeled examples.

evidence.quote: Supervised learning is a machine learning paradigm in which a model learns from labeled examples.

cases.reference_answer: Supervised learning: the model learns from labeled examples, each with input features and a target output.
cases.review_notes: The question avoids the words supervised and labeled.

cases.question: Which way of sharing the processor gives every task a fixed slice of time in turn, and what does that improve?

required_points.text: Round robin assigns each process a fixed time quantum and cycles through ready tasks.

evidence.quote: Round robin assigns each process a fixed time quantum and cycles through ready tasks

required_points.text: It improves responsiveness in time-sharing systems.

evidence.quote: which improves responsiveness in time-sharing systems

cases.reference_answer: Round robin: each process gets a fixed time quantum in turn, which improves responsiveness in time-sharing systems.
cases.review_notes: Both parts required.

cases.question: What does 1NF require?

required_points.text: Each attribute must contain atomic values.

evidence.quote: The first normal form requires that each attribute contain atomic values and that there are no repeating groups.

required_points.text: There must be no repeating groups.

evidence.quote: there are no repeating groups

cases.reference_answer: The first normal form requires atomic attribute values and no repeating groups.
cases.review_notes: The notes write 'first normal form', never '1NF'. Mapping the abbreviation is acceptable; the content must come from the notes.

cases.question: What does the D in ACID stand for, and what does it guarantee?

required_points.text: D stands for durability.

evidence.quote: Durability means that once a transaction is committed, its effects persist even after a crash.

required_points.text: Once a transaction is committed, its effects persist even after a crash.

evidence.quote: once a transaction is committed, its effects persist even after a crash

cases.reference_answer: Durability: once a transaction is committed, its effects persist even after a crash.
cases.review_notes: Both the name and the guarantee are required.

cases.question: Besides locking, which approach to handling concurrency do the notes mention?

required_points.text: Multiversion concurrency control.

evidence.quote: Locking and multiversion concurrency control are two common approaches to handling concurrency.

cases.reference_answer: Multiversion concurrency control.
cases.review_notes: The notes do not explain how it works; an answer that adds a mechanism is ungrounded.

cases.question: Which inter-process communication mechanisms are listed, and why are they needed?

required_points.text: Pipes, sockets and shared memory.

evidence.quote: inter-process communication mechanisms such as pipes, sockets, or shared memory

required_points.text: Because each process has its own memory space, communication between processes usually requires them.

evidence.quote: Because each process has its own memory space, communication between processes usually requires inter-process communication mechanisms

cases.reference_answer: Pipes, sockets and shared memory. Because each process has its own memory space, communication between processes usually requires such mechanisms.
cases.review_notes: Preserve usually (convention C4).

cases.question: Which four counts does a confusion matrix summarize?

required_points.text: True positives, true negatives, false positives and false negatives.

evidence.quote: A confusion matrix summarizes classification results using true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives.

cases.reference_answer: True positives, true negatives, false positives and false negatives.
cases.review_notes: All four are needed for the point.

cases.question: In k-fold cross-validation, how many times does each subset serve as the validation set?

required_points.text: Each subset serves as the validation set once.

evidence.quote: Each subset serves as the validation set once.

cases.reference_answer: Once.
cases.review_notes: Short factual lookup.

cases.question: What does recall measure for a classifier?

required_points.text: Recall measures how many actual positive instances are correctly identified.

evidence.quote: Recall measures how many actual positive instances are correctly identified.

cases.reference_answer: How many actual positive instances are correctly identified.
cases.review_notes: Must not be confused with precision.

cases.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithms are listed as common?

required_points.text: First-come first-served, shortest job first, priority scheduling and round robin.

evidence.quote: Common scheduling algorithms include first-come first-served, shortest job first, priority scheduling, and round robin.

cases.reference_answer: First-come first-served, shortest job first, priority scheduling and round robin.
cases.review_notes: All four are needed for the point.

cases.question: How does regularization help, and which other techniques can help reduce overfitting?

required_points.text: Regularization can reduce variance by discouraging overly complex models.

evidence.quote: Regularization can reduce variance by discouraging overly complex models.

required_points.text: Cross-validation and collecting more data can also help reduce overfitting.

evidence.quote: Techniques such as regularization, cross-validation, and collecting more data can help reduce overfitting.

cases.reference_answer: Regularization can reduce variance by discouraging overly complex models. Cross-validation and collecting more data can also help reduce overfitting.
cases.review_notes: Needs both notes. Preserve can.

cases.question: How are bias and variance related to underfitting and overfitting?

required_points.text: High-bias models are usually too simple and may underfit.

evidence.quote: High-bias models are usually too simple and may underfit the training data.
Underfit models typically have high bias

required_points.text: High-variance models may fit noise in the training set and therefore overfit.

evidence.quote: High-variance models may fit noise in the training set and therefore overfit.

cases.reference_answer: High-bias models are usually too simple and may underfit; high-variance models may fit noise in the training data and overfit.
cases.review_notes: Preserve usually and may.

cases.question: What is the difference between normalization in databases and normalization of features?

required_points.text: In databases, normalization organizes data to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.

evidence.quote: Normalization is the process of organizing data in a relational database to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.

required_points.text: For features, normalization rescales values to a specific range.

evidence.quote: Normalization rescales values to a specific range.

cases.reference_answer: Database normalization organizes relational data to reduce redundancy and improve integrity; feature normalization rescales values to a specific range.
cases.review_notes: Ambiguous term across notes: retrieval must find both.

cases.question: What signs of overfitting do the notes describe?

required_points.text: Performing well on training data but poorly on unseen or test data.

evidence.quote: Overfit models often perform well on training data but poorly on unseen data.
A model that performs very well on training data but poorly on test data is said to be overfitting.

required_points.text: A gap between training accuracy and validation accuracy is often a sign of overfitting.

evidence.quote: A gap between training accuracy and validation accuracy is often a sign of overfitting.

cases.reference_answer: Overfit models often perform well on training data but poorly on unseen data, and a gap between training and validation accuracy is often a sign of overfitting.
cases.review_notes: Preserve often.

cases.question: What role does cross-validation play in evaluating a model?

required_points.text: It estimates how well a model is likely to perform on unseen data (its generalization performance).

evidence.quote: Cross-validation is used to estimate how well a model is likely to perform on unseen data.
It is commonly used to estimate model generalization performance.

required_points.text: It is often used to obtain a more reliable estimate of model performance.

evidence.quote: Cross-validation is often used to obtain a more reliable estimate of model performance.

cases.reference_answer: It estimates how well a model is likely to perform on unseen data and is often used to obtain a more reliable estimate of model performance.
cases.review_notes: Evidence spread over three notes.

cases.question: Why do threads communicate more easily than processes, and what risk does that bring?

required_points.text: Threads of the same process share memory.

evidence.quote: Threads communicate more easily because they share memory.
Threads of the same process share memory and resources, which makes communication between them faster

required_points.text: It introduces risks such as race conditions and synchronization problems.

evidence.quote: it also introduces risks such as race conditions and synchronization problems
also introduces synchronization issues

cases.reference_answer: Threads share memory, so they communicate more easily, but this introduces risks such as race conditions and synchronization problems.
cases.review_notes: Either note supports each point.

cases.question: Which three kinds of anomalies can poorly designed tables cause, and what is a deletion anomaly?

required_points.text: Update, insertion and deletion anomalies.

evidence.quote: which can cause update anomalies, insertion anomalies, and deletion anomalies

required_points.text: A deletion anomaly happens when removing one row accidentally removes other valuable information.

evidence.quote: A deletion anomaly happens when removing one row accidentally removes other valuable information.

cases.reference_answer: Update, insertion and deletion anomalies. A deletion anomaly happens when removing one row accidentally removes other valuable information.
cases.review_notes: Both parts required.

cases.question: What is a transaction, and what does consistency mean in ACID?

required_points.text: A transaction is a logical unit of work that must either complete entirely or have no effect at all.

evidence.quote: A transaction is a logical unit of work that must either complete entirely or have no effect at all.

required_points.text: Consistency means the database moves from one valid state to another valid state.

evidence.quote: Consistency means the database moves from one valid state to another valid state.

cases.reference_answer: A logical unit of work that either completes entirely or has no effect; consistency means the database moves from one valid state to another.
cases.review_notes: Both parts required.

cases.question: What is feature scaling for, and how do normalization and standardization differ?

required_points.text: Feature scaling places features on comparable ranges.

evidence.quote: Feature scaling is commonly used to place features on comparable ranges.

required_points.text: Normalization rescales values to a specific range.

evidence.quote: Normalization rescales values to a specific range.

required_points.text: Standardization transforms values to zero mean and unit variance.

evidence.quote: Standardization transforms values so they have zero mean and unit variance.

cases.reference_answer: Feature scaling places features on comparable ranges. Normalization rescales values to a specific range; standardization gives them zero mean and unit variance.
cases.review_notes: Three points. Must not mix in database normalization.

cases.question: What is the goal of supervised learning, and what does the model minimize during training?

required_points.text: To learn a mapping from inputs to outputs that generalizes to unseen data.

evidence.quote: The goal is to learn a mapping from inputs to outputs so that the model can generalize to unseen data.

required_points.text: A loss function measuring the difference between predictions and true labels.

evidence.quote: During training, the model minimizes a loss function that measures the difference between predictions and true labels.

cases.reference_answer: To learn a mapping from inputs to outputs that generalizes to unseen data; it minimizes a loss function measuring the difference between predictions and true labels.
cases.review_notes: Both parts required.

cases.question: What is multithreading useful for, and which two examples are given?

required_points.text: Applications that perform multiple tasks concurrently.

evidence.quote: Multithreading is useful for applications that perform multiple tasks concurrently

required_points.text: A web server handling multiple client requests, and a program doing background work while keeping the user interface responsive.

evidence.quote: such as a web server handling multiple client requests or a program performing background work while keeping the user interface responsive

cases.reference_answer: Applications that perform multiple tasks concurrently, such as a web server handling many client requests or a program doing background work while keeping its interface responsive.
cases.review_notes: Both examples are needed for the examples point.

cases.question: What is the difference between training error and test error?

required_points.text: Training error refers to performance on the training set.

evidence.quote: Training error refers to performance on the training set

required_points.text: Test error refers to performance on new unseen data.

evidence.quote: test error refers to performance on new unseen data

cases.reference_answer: Training error is performance on the training set; test error is performance on new, unseen data.
cases.review_notes: Both parts required.

cases.question: Does a learning rate that is too large always make gradient descent diverge?

required_points.text: No: the notes say a learning rate that is too large may cause divergence, not that it always does.

evidence.quote: A learning rate that is too large may cause divergence.

cases.reference_answer: The notes say it may cause divergence; they do not say it always does.

cases.question: Are high-bias models always too simple?

evidence.quote: High-bias models are usually too simple and may underfit the training data.

cases.reference_answer: The notes say high-bias models are usually too simple and may underfit, not always.
